hook: Jump into a hole through the Earth, and you'd pop out in thirty-eight minutes.
twist: The textbook answer is 42 minutes, but it assumes Earth has the same density all the way through; with the real, layered Earth (seismic data), Klotz (Am. J. Phys. 2015) gets 38 minutes, and pretending gravity never changes gives almost the same answer.
angle: How long would a fall through the Earth take, and why is the textbook answer wrong?
risks: Pure thought experiment: the page says 'no air, no heat, no spin (simplified)', the paper's own assumptions.
No real person is drawn; the physicist is named in the description only.
